;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**At least 12 people are killed when five [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] gunmen storm a beachfront hotel in [[Mogadishu]] after detonating a [[car bomb]] in front of the building. The attackers were later killed by security forces. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53798834 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**[[Mauritius]] says it will seek "compensation from the owner and the insurer" of MV ''Wakashio'', which broke apart the previous day after leaking hundreds of tonnes of [[fuel oil]]. The [[Japan]]ese company in charge of the ship pledged to compensate for the damage. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53797009 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****The number of deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in [[India]] surpasses 50,000. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-s-covid-death-toll-hits-50-000-mark/story-GcEGRlHivveuLSxfqlqmhJ.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The number of daily new COVID-19 cases in [[South Korea]] tops 200 for the first time in five months, with 279 new cases reported in the last 24 hours. The cases are traced to several conservative [[Christianity in Korea|churches]] in the [[Seoul Capital Area]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southkorea/south-korea-reports-279-coronavirus-cases-most-since-march-idUSKCN25C01M (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Department of Health (Philippines)|Department of Health]] announces a new single-day record-high increase of 40,397 recoveries in the [[Philippines]], bringing the total number of patients discharged to 112,586. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1322495/breaking-doh-reports-new-record-high-40397-recoveries-as-phs-covid-19-cases-top-160k (''Inquirer'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****The [[Florida Department of Health]] reports 3,779 cases, the [[Florida|state]]'s lowest since June 23. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/coronavirus/article244998905.html (''The Miami Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]]
****[[Governor of Georgia|Georgia Governor]] [[Brian Kemp]] signs an executive order that permits local officials to issue [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandates]] in their cities. [https://www.newsweek.com/georgia-governor-allows-local-mask-mandates-first-time-says-they-must-balanced-personal-1525382 (''Newsweek'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
***The government orders the closure of nightclubs and makes masks mandatory for 12 hours between 6:00 p.m. local time and 6:00 a.m. local time. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/16/coronavirus-world-health-organization-reports-daily-record-number-of-covid-19-cases (Euronews)]
*The temperature reaches {{convert|130|F|abbr=on|1}} in [[Death Valley]], [[California]] amidst a historic heat wave in the western United States. If verified, it is the hottest temperature recorded on Earth in the month of August, and the hottest in any month since 1931. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/weather/2020/08/16/death-valley-heat-record/ (''The Washington Post'')]

;International relations
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Russia]] says it is "ready to assist Belarus in accordance with a collective military pact if necessary" as opposition leader in-exile [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] calls for a massive march. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election/putin-says-ready-to-help-belarus-president-militarily-if-necessary-idUSKCN25C08E?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–United Arab Emirates peace agreement]]
**The [[United Arab Emirates]] unblocks telephone lines between the country and [[Israel]], as well as allowing people in the country to access Israeli websites. Israeli Communications Minister [[Yoaz Hendel]] congratulates the [[Government of the United Arab Emirates|Emirati government]] for the move. [https://apnews.com/3b898c7b6852af9de09617381dc3f540 (AP)]
*[[Iran–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**The Emirati government summons the [[government of Iran|Iranian]] ''[[chargé d'affaires]]'' in [[Abu Dhabi]] to protest a speech by [[President of Iran|Iranian President]] [[Hassan Rouhani]] which called the UAE's peace agreement with Israel "a treacherous act." The Emirati government labeled these remarks as "unacceptable, inflammatory and carrying serious repercussions for the security and stability of the Arabian Gulf region." [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/gulf/2020/08/16/UAE-summons-Iranian-Charge-d-Affaires-in-Abu-Dhabi-WAM-.html (Al Arabiya)]

;Politics and elections
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
*****[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
******Hundreds of [[GCE Advanced Level]] students protest outside the [[Department for Education]] headquarters in [[London]] demanding for a reassessment of their final-year performance by the [[Ofqual]], which has used an algorithm to assess students' performances in lieu of the exams that were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics claim the Ofqual's algorithm to be "flawed" as the grades issued differ significantly from those predicted by teachers. [[Secretary of State for Education|Education Secretary]] [[Gavin Williamson]] had issued a statement clarifying that students may use their teacher's predicted grades or results from any trial exam, although the Ofqual issued a separate statement favouring teacher evaluations over trial exams. Students are requesting for an intervention from [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]]. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3097588/british-prime-minister-boris-johnson-under-fire-amid-growing (AP via ''SCMP'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
*****Hundreds of protesters at the [[Plaza de Colón]] in [[Madrid]] demand the [[Government of Spain|government]] rescinds the compulsory [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|wearing of face masks]] in public, which had been imposed following the resurgence of COVID-19 cases in July. Protesters claim that such restrictions are an attempt by the government to curtail people's freedoms. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/hundreds-protest-in-madrid-against-coronavirus-restrictions (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[2020 New Zealand general election]]
****Prime Minister [[Jacinda Ardern]] postpones the upcoming general election from 19 September to 17 October due to a recent resurgence of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/122466319/live-jacinda-ardern-delays-election-to-october-17-amid-coronavirus-outbreak (Stuff)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/16/asia/new-zealand-election-delay-coronavrius/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Tens of thousands protest in the Belarusian capital [[Minsk]] calling for [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] to step down. It is believed to be the largest protest in [[History of Belarus|Belarusian history]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/16/belarus-prepares-for-biggest-protest-yet-after-week-of-anger (''The Guardian'')]
**In a defiant speech, Alexander Lukashenko addresses supporters in [[Independence Square, Minsk]], where he claims Belarus would "die as a state" if new elections were held, and accuses [[NATO]] of "massing on the border". Opposition critics say most of those at the rally were coerced into attending and had been bussed in from other parts of the country. [https://news.sky.com/story/belarus-president-lukashenko-claims-nato-massing-on-border-and-denies-election-was-rigged-12050451 (Sky News)]
**The Belarusian Ambassador to [[Slovakia]], Igor Leshchenya, defects to the [[Belarusian democracy movement|opposition]] after posting a video declaring his support for the protests. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/belarus-protests-ambassador-alexander-lukashenko-nasha-niva-slovakia-a9672771.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2020 Thai protests]]
**More than 10,000 people march against the [[government of Thailand|government]], demanding their [[resignation]] and a curb to its [[monarchy of Thailand|monarchy]]'s power. The protesters also demand a change in the [[constitution of Thailand|constitution]]. Meanwhile, dozens held pro-monarchy counter-protests. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/thousands-protest-bangkok-demanding-gov-resignation-200816094356179.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Politics of the Dominican Republic]]
**[[Luis Abinader]] is sworn in as [[President of the Dominican Republic|President]] after winning the [[2020 Dominican Republic general election|2020 general elections]]. He succeeds [[Danilo Medina]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2020/08/16/world/americas/ap-cb-dominican-republic-us.html?searchResultPosition=5 (''The New York Times'')]
